1.1: After Joshua passed, the Israelites went to God and asked, 'Aight Lord, who goin' up first to fight these Canaanites for us?'
1.2: And the Lord said, 'Judah got this. I already put the land in his hands.'
1.3: So Judah hit up his bro Simeon like, 'Yo, roll with me to my spot so we can take down these Canaanites. If you got me, I got you when it's your turn.' And Simeon was down.
1.4: Judah stepped up, and the Lord let them wreck shop on the Canaanites and the Perizzites—took out 10,000 men in Bezek.
1.5: That's where they found Adoni-Bezek, went toe-to-toe with him, and straight-up crushed the Canaanites and Perizzites.
1.6: Adoni-Bezek tried to dip, but they caught him and cut off his thumbs and big toes.
1.7: Adoni-Bezek was like, 'Man, 70 kings had to scrape for food under my table 'cause I did 'em dirty like this. Now God done hit me back the same way.' Then they took him to Jerusalem, and that's where he died.
1.8: Judah's squad went in on Jerusalem, took it over, hit it with the sword, and set the whole city on fire.
1.9: After that, Judah's folks went after more Canaanites—ones in the mountains, down south, and in the lowlands.
1.10: Then they came for the Canaanites in Hebron, back when it was called Kirjath Arba. They handled Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
1.11: Next, they pulled up on the people in Debir, which used to be called Kirjath Sepher.
1.12: Caleb put it out there, 'Whoever takes down Kirjath Sepher, I'ma give 'em my daughter Achsah as a wife.'
1.13: Othniel, Kenaz's son and Caleb's younger bro, went ahead and did it, so Caleb gave him Achsah.
1.14: When Achsah got with Othniel, she told him, 'Ask my pops for some land.' She pulled up on Caleb, hopped off her donkey, and he was like, 'What's up?'
1.15: She said, 'Bless me real quick—since you already gave me dry land, hook me up with some water too.' And Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs.
1.16: The Kenites, Moses' in-laws, left Jericho with Judah's people and settled in the wilderness of Judah, down south near Arad.
1.17: Then Judah and Simeon linked up again, ran up on Zephath, and completely wiped it out. That's why they renamed the place Hormah.
1.18: Judah also took over Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron, plus all their surrounding land.
1.19: The Lord was with Judah, and they pushed back the mountain folks. But they couldn't handle the people in the lowlands 'cause they had iron chariots.
1.20: Like Moses said, they gave Hebron to Caleb, and he kicked out the three sons of Anak.
1.21: But the tribe of Benjamin didn't drive out the Jebusites in Jerusalem, so they still there living with Benjamin's people to this day.
1.22: The house of Joseph went up against Bethel, and the Lord was rocking with them.
1.23: They sent some men to spy on Bethel, which used to be called Luz.
1.24: The spies saw a man leaving the city and told him, 'Yo, show us a way in, and we'll look out for you.'
1.25: Dude showed them the entrance, and they took over the city, wiping it out with swords—but they let him and his fam go.
1.26: That man dipped to the land of the Hittites, built a new city, and called it Luz, and that's what it's still called.
1.27: But Manasseh didn't clear out the folks in Beth Shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, or Megiddo—the Canaanites held their ground.
1.28: When Israel got stronger, they made the Canaanites pay taxes, but they never fully kicked them out.
1.29: Ephraim didn't get rid of the Canaanites in Gezer either, so they stayed living among them.
1.30: Same with Zebulun—Kitron and Nahalol still had Canaanites in them, and they just put them under taxes.
1.31: Asher didn't drive out the people from Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
1.32: So instead of the Canaanites moving out, Asher's people just lived among them.
1.33: Naphtali did the same with the folks in Beth Shemesh and Beth Anath. They didn't take over completely, just taxed them.
1.34: Meanwhile, the Amorites straight up pushed the tribe of Dan into the mountains and wouldn't let them come down into the valley.
1.35: The Amorites held strong in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when Joseph's house got stronger, they put them under tribute too.
1.36: The border of the Amorites ran from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and upward.

2.1: Then the Angel of the Lord pulled up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, 'Look, I brought y'all outta Egypt, set y'all up in the land I promised your ancestors, and told y'all straight up—I ain't never breaking my covenant with you.'
2.2: 'I told y'all not to be making no deals with these folks in this land. Tear down their altars, don't mix with 'em. But what y'all do? Y'all ain't listen. Why you gotta do me like this?'
2.3: 'So now, since y'all ain't listen, I ain't clearing these folks out for you. They gon' stay right here, be a thorn in your side, and their gods gon' trap you up.'
2.4: When the Angel of the Lord finished speaking to all Israel, the people broke down crying, loud as ever.
2.5: They called that spot Bochim, which means 'weeping,' and they sacrificed to the Lord right there.
2.6: After Joshua let everybody go, the Israelites went back to claim their land and settle in.
2.7: The people kept serving the Lord as long as Joshua was alive, and even while the elders that came up with him were still around—those who had seen with their own eyes all the great things the Lord did for Israel.
2.8: Then Joshua, son of Nun, the Lord's servant, died at 110 years old.
2.9: They buried him in his land at Timnath Heres, up in the mountains of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
2.10: And after that whole generation was gone, a new generation came up who ain't know the Lord or all the stuff He did for Israel.
2.11: Then the Israelites started acting up—doing evil in the Lord's sight and serving these weak little Baal gods.
2.12: They straight up abandoned the God of their ancestors, the one who freed them from Egypt, and started chasing after these fake gods from the nations around 'em. Bowing down to 'em, worshipping 'em—making the Lord real mad.
2.13: They turned their backs on the Lord and started serving Baal and Ashtoreth, getting caught up in all that idol mess.
2.14: So the Lord got heated. He let raiders come through, take their stuff, and handed them over to their enemies. They couldn't even stand up against them.
2.15: Everywhere they went, the Lord's hand was against them. Just like He warned 'em, they were catching nothing but L's and ended up real miserable.
2.16: But even then, the Lord had mercy and raised up judges to help rescue them from the folks that was doing 'em dirty.
2.17: But nope, they ain't wanna listen to the judges either. Instead, they ran after these other gods, bowing down and wildin' out. They turned away from how their ancestors lived, ignoring God's commandments like it was nothing.
2.18: But every time the Lord put a judge in place, He was with them. As long as the judge was alive, He made sure Israel was good. He had compassion on them 'cause He heard their cries from all the trouble they was in.
2.19: But the second that judge died? They went right back to acting worse than before. Chasing after these false gods, bowing down, being hardheaded, and refusing to change their ways.
2.20: So the Lord got fed up and said, 'Since y'all keep breaking my covenant and ignoring my commands…'
2.21: 'I'm done clearing out these nations for y'all. The ones Joshua ain't get rid of before he died? They staying right here.'
2.22: 'Let's see if Israel will actually stick to my ways and live how their ancestors did, or if they gon' keep messing up.'
2.23: So the Lord left those nations where they were. He didn't clear 'em out right away, and He ain't give them over to Joshua neither.

3.1: These the nations the Lord left behind to test Israel—to see what the new generation, who ain't been in those Canaan battles, was really about.
3.2: (He did this to teach the next generation how to fight since they ain't have no war experience before.)
3.3: These were the ones left: five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living up in Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
3.4: God left them there to see if Israel would actually follow His commandments like He told their ancestors through Moses.
3.5: But instead of driving them out, Israel started living among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
3.6: They started intermarrying—giving their daughters to these folks and taking their daughters as wives. Next thing you know, they out here serving their gods.
3.7: Israel started acting up again, doing evil in the Lord's sight. They straight up forgot about the Lord and started worshipping Baal and Asherah.
3.8: So God got fed up and handed them over to Cushan-Rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia. Israel ended up serving him for eight years.
3.9: Then Israel cried out to the Lord, and He raised up a deliverer for them—Othniel, the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
3.10: The Spirit of the Lord came on Othniel, and he became Israel's judge. He led them into battle, and the Lord helped him take down Cushan-Rishathaim, giving him the W.
3.11: And just like that, the land had peace for 40 years. Then Othniel died.
3.12: But as soon as Othniel was gone, Israel started wildin' again, doing evil in the Lord's sight. So the Lord let Eglon, king of Moab, rise up against them because of their sins.
3.13: Eglon linked up with the Ammonites and Amalekites, came through, put Israel in a chokehold, and took over the City of Palms.
3.14: Israel was stuck serving Eglon, king of Moab, for eighteen years.
3.15: But when they finally cried out to the Lord, He raised up a deliverer—Ehud, the son of Gera from the tribe of Benjamin, a left-handed warrior. Israel sent him to bring tribute money to King Eglon.
3.16: Ehud had a plan, though. He made himself a double-edged dagger, about a foot and a half long, and strapped it under his clothes on his right thigh.
3.17: He brought the tribute to Eglon, who, by the way, was a very heavy man.
3.18: After dropping off the tribute, Ehud sent the other guys who helped carry it back home.
3.19: Then he doubled back from the stone idols at Gilgal and told Eglon, 'Yo, King, I got a secret message for you.' Eglon was intrigued and told his attendants to leave.
3.20: Ehud came up close while Eglon was chilling in his private upstairs room. Then Ehud said, 'I got a message straight from God for you.' Eglon stood up from his seat.
3.21: That's when Ehud, quick as ever, pulled his dagger from his right thigh with his left hand and drove it straight into Eglon's belly.
3.22: The whole dagger went in deep, handle and all, and the fat closed over it. Ehud ain't even pull the blade out—Eglon's guts spilled everywhere.
3.23: Ehud dipped out through the porch, locked the doors behind him, and got away.
3.24: After he left, Eglon's servants came by and saw the doors locked. They figured, 'Oh, he probably just using the bathroom in there.'
3.25: They waited. And waited. Until they got embarrassed 'cause he was taking way too long. Finally, they grabbed the key, unlocked the doors, and—boom—found their king dead on the floor.
3.26: Meanwhile, Ehud had already escaped, passed the stone images, and made it to Seirah.
3.27: As soon as he got there, he blew the trumpet in the mountains of Ephraim, rallying the Israelites to rise up.
3.28: He told them, 'Let's go! The Lord done handed the Moabites over to us!' So they followed him, took control of the Jordan crossings, and let nobody escape.
3.29: They wiped out 10,000 Moabite warriors that day—all strong, capable fighters. Not a single one got away.
3.30: And just like that, Moab was humbled under Israel's rule. The land stayed peaceful for 80 years.
3.31: After Ehud, there was Shamgar, the son of Anath. This man took an ox goad (basically a long stick) and used it to kill 600 Philistines by himself. And just like that, he saved Israel.

4.1: After Ehud died, Israel started acting up again, doing evil in the Lord's sight.
4.2: So the Lord let them get taken over by Jabin, king of Canaan, who ruled from Hazor. His top general was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth Hagoyim.
4.3: Israel cried out to God 'cause Jabin had 900 iron chariots and had been oppressing them hard for 20 years.
4.4: Now at that time, Deborah, a prophetess and wife of Lapidoth, was judging Israel.
4.5: She would sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came to her to settle their disputes.
4.6: One day she sent for Barak, son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali, and told him, 'Didn't the Lord tell you to get your troops together? Go post up at Mount Tabor with 10,000 men from Naphtali and Zebulun.'
4.7: 'Sisera, Jabin's general, gon' roll up on y'all by the Kishon River with his army and chariots. But don't trip—God already set it up for you to win.'
4.8: Barak said, 'I'll go… but only if you go with me!'
4.9: Deborah was like, 'Bet, I'll go. But just so you know, you ain't getting no credit for this victory—God gon' hand Sisera over to a woman.' So Deborah rolled with Barak to Kedesh.
4.10: Barak called up the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, and 10,000 men followed him. Deborah was right there with him.
4.11: Meanwhile, Heber the Kenite, from Moses' in-law's family, had split off from his people and set up camp near the oak tree at Zaanaim, close to Kedesh.
4.12: Sisera got the word that Barak was up at Mount Tabor.
4.13: So he rounded up all 900 iron chariots and his whole army and headed to the Kishon River, ready for war.
4.14: Then Deborah told Barak, 'Aight, time to move! Today's the day the Lord is handing Sisera over to you. You already know He went ahead of you!'
4.15: So Barak charged down from Mount Tabor with his 10,000 men, and the Lord threw Sisera's army into chaos. Barak's squad ran through them with the sword, and Sisera had to jump out his chariot and take off on foot.
4.16: Barak and his men chased the enemy all the way back to Harosheth Hagoyim. By the time it was over, every single one of Sisera's soldiers was dead.
4.17: Sisera, meanwhile, ran off to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite. Since Heber's people had a peace treaty with Jabin, Sisera thought he was safe.
4.18: Jael stepped out to meet him and said, 'Come in, my lord, don't be scared.' So he went in, and she covered him up with a blanket.
4.19: He told her, 'Please, I'm mad thirsty—gimme some water.' But instead of water, she gave him some milk, then tucked him in real good.
4.20: Then Sisera said, 'Stand at the tent door, and if anybody asks if I'm in here, tell 'em no.'
4.21: But while he was knocked out, Jael grabbed a tent peg and a hammer, crept up on him, and drove that peg straight through his skull into the ground. Dude ain't even wake up—he was gone.
4.22: When Barak came looking for Sisera, Jael stepped out and said, 'I got who you looking for.' He stepped inside and saw Sisera laid out, dead, with a tent peg through his head.
4.23: And just like that, God humbled Jabin, the king of Canaan, right in front of Israel.
4.24: From that day forward, Israel kept pressing harder and harder against Jabin until they completely wiped him out.

5.1: On that day, Deborah and Barak, son of Abinoam, sang this song:
5.2: 'When the leaders step up, and the people willingly follow, bless the Lord!'
5.3: 'Listen up, kings! Pay attention, rulers! I'ma sing to the Lord, I'ma praise the Lord, the God of Israel!'
5.4: 'Lord, when You stepped out from Seir, when You marched from Edom's fields, the earth shook, the heavens opened up, and the clouds let loose rain.'
5.5: 'The mountains trembled before You, Lord, yes, even Mount Sinai before the God of Israel!'
5.6: 'Back in the days of Shamgar, son of Anath, and in Jael's time, the highways were empty—travelers had to take the backroads just to be safe.'
5.7: 'Village life straight-up stopped in Israel, until I, Deborah, stood up, stood up like a mother to Israel.'
5.8: 'They went and chose new gods, and what happened? War came right to their gates. But not a single shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel.'
5.9: 'My heart is with the leaders of Israel, the ones who stepped up and stood with the people. Bless the Lord!'
5.10: 'Y'all who ride on white donkeys, y'all who wear fine clothes and sit in judgment—speak on this!'
5.11: 'By the wells, far from the battle cries, they gon' tell the stories of the Lord's victories, how He saved His people. Then the Lord's people will come down to the gates!'
5.12: 'Wake up, wake up, Deborah! Wake up, wake up and sing! Get up, Barak! Lead your captives away, son of Abinoam!'
5.13: 'Then the survivors of Israel rose up, and the Lord sent them against the mighty.'
5.14: 'From Ephraim came warriors, tracing back to Amalek. Benjamin's people followed close behind. From Machir came leaders, from Zebulun, those who carry the commander's staff.'
5.15: 'The princes of Issachar were with Deborah; they rode with Barak, charging into the valley. But Reuben? Man, y'all hesitated!'
5.16: 'Why y'all still chillin' by the sheep pens, listening to the shepherds play their flutes? Reuben was over there debating when the fight was already on!'
5.17: 'Gilead stayed put on the other side of the Jordan. And Dan? Still out at sea. Asher was relaxing on the coast, posted up by the shores.'
5.18: 'But Zebulun? Naphtali? They put their lives on the line in the heat of battle.'
5.19: 'The kings of Canaan pulled up, fought hard at Taanach, by Megiddo's waters. But guess what? They ain't win nothing—not even silver for their trouble!'
5.20: 'Even the stars up in the sky fought against Sisera, working against him from the heavens!'
5.21: 'The Kishon River swept them away—that old, mighty river, Kishon. March on, my soul, with strength!'
5.22: 'Then the enemy's horses were galloping, their mighty steeds pounding the ground in retreat.'
5.23: 'Curse Meroz!' said the angel of the Lord. 'Curse the people there bad, 'cause they ain't come help the Lord fight the strong ones!'
5.24: 'Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite—blessed among all the tent-dwelling women!'
5.25: 'Sisera asked her for water, but she gave him milk. She brought it in a royal cup, playing the part so smooth.'
5.26: 'Then she grabbed that tent peg with one hand, the workman's hammer in the other. She crushed his skull, smashed his temple, drove that peg straight through!'
5.27: 'At her feet, he sank down. He fell. He lay still. At her feet, he sank, he fell. Right where he dropped, that's where he died.'
5.28: 'Meanwhile, Sisera's mama was looking out the window, crying through the curtains: 'Why is his chariot taking so long? Why don't I hear his horses coming?''
5.29: 'Her ladies tried to reassure her, and even she told herself: '
5.30: 'Oh, they must be dividing the spoils! Each soldier getting a woman or two. Sisera getting embroidered cloth, fancy dyed garments, rich robes for the victor!'
5.31: 'But Lord, let all Your enemies perish like that! And let those who love You shine bright like the sun at full strength!'
5.32: And just like that, the land had peace for forty years.

6.1: Once again, Israel started acting up, doing evil in the Lord's sight. So the Lord let the Midianites run them for seven years.
6.2: Midian had them so shook that the Israelites started hiding out in caves, mountains, and strongholds just to stay safe.
6.3: Every time Israel planted crops, the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern tribes would roll up on them.
6.4: They'd camp out, wreck the fields all the way to Gaza, and leave Israel with nothing—no food, no sheep, no oxen, no donkeys.
6.5: Midian and their crew came in like locusts, deep with camels and everything. It was so many of them, they basically overran the land just to destroy it.
6.6: Israel was struggling hard because of Midian, so they finally cried out to the Lord for help.
6.7: When Israel called out to God about Midian, He sent a prophet to check them.
6.8: The prophet told them, 'This what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: I brought y'all up out of Egypt, out of slavery.'
6.9: 'I saved y'all from the Egyptians and everybody else who was messing with you. I drove them out and gave y'all their land.'
6.10: 'I told y'all, "I am the Lord your God. Don't be out here fearing these Amorite gods in whose land you living now." But what did y'all do? You ain't listen.'
6.11: One day, the Angel of the Lord pulled up and sat under the terebinth tree in Ophrah, where Joash the Abiezrite lived. His son Gideon was hiding in a winepress, trying to thresh wheat so the Midianites wouldn't catch him.
6.12: Then the Angel of the Lord appeared to him and said, 'The Lord is with you, mighty warrior!'
6.13: Gideon was like, 'Man, if the Lord is really with us, then why is all this happening? Where are all the miracles our ancestors told us about—how He brought them out of Egypt? Right now, it just feel like He left us hanging, handing us over to Midian.'
6.14: The Lord looked at him and said, 'Go with the strength you got and save Israel from the Midianites. Didn't I send you?'
6.15: But Gideon was like, 'Lord, how am I supposed to save Israel? My family is the weakest in Manasseh, and I'm the least important in my whole house!'
6.16: The Lord said, 'I'll be with you. And trust me, you gon' take Midian down like they just one man.'
6.17: Gideon said, 'Alright then, if I really got favor with You, prove it—give me a sign that it's really You talking to me.'
6.18: 'Hold on right here till I come back with an offering.' And the Lord was like, 'Aight, I'll wait.'
6.19: Gideon ran inside, prepped a young goat and some unleavened bread with an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket, the broth in a pot, and brought it back under the tree.
6.20: The Angel of God said, 'Put the meat and bread on this rock and pour out the broth.' So Gideon did it.
6.21: Then the Angel of the Lord touched the food with His staff—BOOM—fire shot up from the rock and burned it all up. And just like that, the Angel disappeared.
6.22: That's when Gideon realized, 'Oh snap! That was really the Angel of the Lord!' He panicked and said, 'Lord God, I done seen the Angel of the Lord face to face!'
6.23: But the Lord said, 'Calm down. Peace be with you. You ain't gon' die.'
6.24: So Gideon built an altar there and called it The Lord is Peace. And that altar still standing in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
6.25: That night, the Lord told Gideon, 'Take your daddy's bull, the second one that's seven years old. Tear down your father's altar to Baal, and cut down the Asherah pole next to it.'
6.26: 'Then build an altar to the Lord your God on top of this rock in the right way. Use the wood from the Asherah pole to burn the bull as a sacrifice.'
6.27: Gideon grabbed ten of his servants and did what the Lord said. But he was too scared of his family and the city folks to do it in broad daylight, so he did it at night.
6.28: Next morning, the town woke up and saw Baal's altar destroyed, the Asherah pole chopped down, and the bull burning on a new altar.
6.29: They started asking around, 'Who did this?' After some investigation, they found out it was Gideon, son of Joash.
6.30: The men of the city went to Joash and said, 'Bring your son out here! He gotta die for tearing down Baal's altar and cutting down that Asherah pole!'
6.31: But Joash clapped back, 'Y'all really out here fighting for Baal? Y'all need to save him? If Baal is really a god, let him handle his own business! If anybody wanna fight for Baal, they better be dead by morning!'
6.32: That day, they started calling Gideon Jerubbaal, meaning 'Let Baal handle him,' since he tore down Baal's altar.
6.33: Not long after, the Midianites, Amalekites, and the other eastern people grouped up, crossed over, and set up camp in the Valley of Jezreel.
6.34: Then the Spirit of the Lord took over Gideon. He blew the trumpet, calling his clan, the Abiezrites, to follow him.
6.35: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they all came to join him.
6.36: Gideon said to God, 'If You really gonna use me to save Israel like You said…'
6.37: 'I'ma put this fleece of wool out on the ground. If in the morning the fleece is wet but the ground is dry, then I'll know You really got me on this.'
6.38: And sure enough, the next morning, Gideon wrung out a bowlful of water from the fleece while the ground stayed dry.
6.39: But Gideon wasn't done. 'Lord, don't be mad at me, but let me check one more time. This time, let the fleece stay dry, but the ground be covered in dew.'
6.40: That night, God did exactly that—fleece was bone dry, but the whole ground was soaked.

7.1: Early in the morning, Jerubbaal (a.k.a. Gideon) and his crew camped near the well of Harod. Meanwhile, the Midianites were posted up north of them in the valley by the hill of Moreh.
7.2: Then the Lord told Gideon, 'Bruh, you got too many people with you. If y'all win like this, Israel gon' start acting like they did it all on their own and not give Me the credit.'
7.3: 'So go tell 'em: If anybody scared, they can go home right now.' And just like that, 22,000 of them dipped. Only 10,000 stayed.
7.4: But the Lord said, 'Still too many. Take them down to the water—I'ma test them for you there. I'll tell you who stays and who goes.'
7.5: So Gideon brought them to the water, and the Lord said, 'Separate the ones who scoop water with their hands and lap it up like a dog from the ones who kneel to drink.'
7.6: Only 300 men drank from their hands. The rest kneeled to drink straight from the stream.
7.7: Then the Lord said, 'Aight, these 300 right here? They the ones. I'ma hand Midian over to you through them. Send everybody else home.'
7.8: So the 300 stayed, taking supplies and trumpets, while the rest went home. Meanwhile, the Midianites were still camped out below in the valley.
7.9: That same night, the Lord told Gideon, 'Get up, go attack the camp—I already gave them to you.'
7.10: 'But if you nervous, take your boy Purah and go eavesdrop on them first.'
7.11: 'Listen to what they saying, and I promise it'll hype you up for battle.' So Gideon and Purah snuck down near the enemy's outpost.
7.12: Midianites, Amalekites, and all the eastern people were deep in that valley, as thick as locusts. Their camels alone were countless, like the sand on the seashore.
7.13: As Gideon got closer, he heard one soldier telling his homie a dream: 'Man, I had this wild dream—a barley loaf rolled into our camp, hit a tent, flipped it over, and the whole thing collapsed!'
7.14: His friend was like, 'Oh snap, that's gotta mean Gideon, son of Joash, is about to take us down. God already gave Midian to him!'
7.15: When Gideon heard that, he bowed in worship. Then he ran back to camp and said, 'Get up! The Lord already handed Midian over to us!'
7.16: Gideon split his 300 men into three groups. He gave each of them a trumpet, an empty jar, and a torch hidden inside the jar.
7.17: He told them, 'Watch me. Do exactly what I do. When we get to the edge of the camp, follow my lead.'
7.18: 'When I blow my trumpet, all of y'all blow yours too and shout, "The sword of the Lord and of Gideon!"'
7.19: So Gideon and 100 of his men rolled up to the enemy camp just as the night guards were changing shifts.
7.20: All three groups blew their trumpets, smashed their jars, grabbed their torches, and yelled, 'The sword of the Lord and of Gideon!'
7.21: Nobody moved—just stood their ground while the enemy camp went into full panic mode, running around screaming.
7.22: Then when the 300 blew their trumpets, the Lord made the enemy turn on each other with their own swords. They started fighting themselves and ran toward Beth Acacia, Zererah, and as far as the border of Abel Meholah near Tabbath.
7.23: Meanwhile, men from Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh gathered up and chased Midian down.
7.24: Gideon sent messengers to the Ephraimites, telling them, 'Come through and cut off the Midianites at the Jordan and Beth Barah!'
7.25: So the men of Ephraim caught up, blocked them off, and captured Midian's two princes, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the Rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the Winepress of Zeeb. And just to make sure Gideon knew, they brought him the heads of Oreb and Zeeb across the Jordan.

8.1: Then the men of Ephraim came at Gideon like, 'Bruh, why you ain't call us when you went to fight Midian? You just left us out like that?' They was heated.
8.2: Gideon hit 'em back like, 'Chill, y'all did more than me! Ain't Ephraim's leftovers better than all of Abiezer's best?'
8.3: 'Y'all the ones who took down Oreb and Zeeb, the Midianite princes. What I did don't even compare to that!' And just like that, they calmed down.
8.4: Gideon and his 300 men crossed the Jordan, exhausted but still chasing Midian.
8.5: They got to Succoth, and Gideon was like, 'Yo, can y'all give my people some bread? We tired, but we still hunting Zebah and Zalmunna, Midian's kings.'
8.6: The leaders of Succoth were like, 'You ain't caught 'em yet, so why should we help?'
8.7: Gideon snapped back, 'Aight bet—when I do catch 'em, I'ma come back and tear y'all up with desert thorns and briers!'
8.8: Then he went to Penuel and asked the same thing, but they disrespected him too.
8.9: So he told them, 'When I come back in peace, I'ma tear this whole tower down!'
8.10: Meanwhile, Zebah and Zalmunna were chillin' in Karkor with about 15,000 men—only ones left from an army that started at 120,000.
8.11: Gideon pulled up through a back route, sneaking up from the east, past Nobah and Jogbehah. The enemy wasn't even ready for it.
8.12: Zebah and Zalmunna tried to run, but Gideon chased 'em down, captured them, and wrecked the rest of their army.
8.13: After the battle, Gideon came back through the Ascent of Heres.
8.14: He caught a young man from Succoth, made him write down the names of their 77 leaders.
8.15: Then he rolled up to Succoth and said, 'Remember when y'all clowned me, saying I ain't caught Zebah and Zalmunna? Well, here they go!'
8.16: Then he grabbed the city elders, got some thorns and briers, and taught them a painful lesson.
8.17: Then he went to Penuel, tore down their tower like he promised, and killed the men of the city.
8.18: Then he asked Zebah and Zalmunna, 'The men y'all killed at Tabor, what did they look like?'
8.19: They said, 'Man, they looked like you—like sons of a king.'
8.20: Gideon was like, 'Yeah, 'cause they was my brothers. If y'all had spared them, I wouldn't be killing you now.' Then he told his son Jether, 'Go ahead, take 'em out!'
8.21: But Jether hesitated—he was young and too scared to do it. So Zebah and Zalmunna said, 'Man, if you really bout it, do it yourself!' So Gideon handled it and took the royal ornaments off their camels' necks.
8.22: After all that, Israel came to Gideon like, 'You the man! Rule over us—you, your son, and your grandson. You saved us from Midian!'
8.23: But Gideon was like, 'Nah, I ain't ruling over y'all, and neither will my son. The Lord is your ruler.'
8.24: 'But I do got one request—everybody drop one gold earring from the loot y'all took.' (The Midianites wore gold earrings 'cause they were Ishmaelites.)
8.25: They said, 'Bet, we got you!' and spread out a cloth, throwing in their gold earrings.
8.26: Altogether, Gideon got 1,700 shekels of gold—not counting the royal chains, pendants, and purple robes from Midian's kings, plus the gold chains from their camels.
8.27: Gideon took all that gold and made an ephod, setting it up in his hometown, Ophrah. But Israel started worshipping it, and it became a trap for Gideon and his fam.
8.28: Still, Midian got humbled. They never rose up again, and Israel had peace for 40 years while Gideon was alive.
8.29: After all that, Gideon (Jerubbaal) went back home.
8.30: Bruh had 70 sons—dude had a lot of wives.
8.31: He even had a side chick in Shechem who gave him a son named Abimelech.
8.32: Eventually, Gideon died of old age and was buried in his father Joash's tomb in Ophrah.
8.33: But the second Gideon was gone, Israel started acting up again—going right back to worshipping Baal and making Baal-Berith their god.
8.34: They straight up forgot about the Lord, the One who saved them from all their enemies.
8.35: And they ain't even show love to Gideon's family, despite all the good he did for them.

9.1: Abimelech, Gideon's son, rolled up to Shechem, went to his uncles and his mama's family, and said,
9.2: 'Y'all gotta decide—what's better? Having all seventy of Gideon's sons ruling over you, or just one? And don't forget, I'm your own flesh and blood!'
9.3: His uncles spread the word, hyping him up to the men of Shechem, and they were like, 'Yeah, he our brother. Let's roll with him.'
9.4: So they gave him seventy shekels of silver from Baal-Berith's temple, and he used that money to hire a crew of wild, reckless dudes to follow him.
9.5: Then he went to his daddy's house in Ophrah and killed all seventy of his brothers on one stone. But the youngest, Jotham, managed to hide and escape.
9.6: The men of Shechem and Beth Millo got together and crowned Abimelech king by the big tree near the pillar in Shechem.
9.7: When Jotham heard what happened, he climbed up Mount Gerizim and yelled, 'Listen up, men of Shechem! If y'all hear me, maybe God will hear y'all too!'
9.8: 'One day, the trees wanted a king. They went to the olive tree and said, "Rule over us!"'
9.9: 'But the olive tree said, "Why would I stop making oil that honors God and people just to wave around over some trees?"'
9.10: 'Then they went to the fig tree, saying, "Come be our king!"'
9.11: 'But the fig tree said, "Why would I stop making sweet fruit just to rule over y'all?"'
9.12: 'Next, they asked the grapevine, "Come be our king!"'
9.13: 'The vine said, "Why would I stop making wine that brings joy to God and people just to wave over y'all?"'
9.14: 'Finally, they went to the bramble bush and said, "You come and rule over us!"'
9.15: 'The bramble said, "If y'all really want me as king, then come sit in my shade. But if not, may fire come from me and burn down the mighty cedars of Lebanon!"'
9.16: 'So if y'all really did right by Gideon's family when y'all made Abimelech king, then cool, enjoy him.'
9.17: 'But don't forget—my father fought for y'all, risked his life, and saved y'all from Midian.'
9.18: 'And this how y'all repay him? Killing his seventy sons and putting this dude, the son of a servant woman, in charge just 'cause he's your kin?'
9.19: 'If y'all did right by Gideon, cool. But if not, may fire come from Abimelech and burn y'all up, and may fire come from y'all and burn him up!'
9.21: Then Jotham took off running, dipped to Beer, and stayed low 'cause he knew Abimelech was coming for him.
9.22: Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.
9.23: But then, God sent bad blood between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and they turned on him.
9.24: This was God paying them back for what they did to Gideon's seventy sons. Both Abimelech and the Shechemites had blood on their hands.
9.25: Shechem's people started setting up ambushes in the hills, robbing everybody passing through. Somebody told Abimelech what was going on.
9.26: Then a dude named Gaal, son of Ebed, rolled into Shechem with his brothers, and the people started rocking with him instead.
9.27: They went to their vineyards, crushed grapes, made wine, got lit, and started talking crazy about Abimelech at their false god's temple.
9.28: Gaal started popping off: 'Who is Abimelech, and why should we serve him? Ain't he just Gideon's son? And ain't Zebul just his officer? We should be serving the real leaders of Shechem's past!'
9.29: 'Man, if I was in charge, I'd handle Abimelech real quick!' Then he said, 'Come on, Abimelech! Bring your army and let's settle this!'
9.30: Zebul, the city's governor, heard Gaal running his mouth and got mad.
9.31: He secretly sent messengers to Abimelech, saying, 'Yo, Gaal and his people are hyping the city against you!'
9.32: 'You better move tonight, take your soldiers, and ambush the city.'
9.33: 'At sunrise, rush in and handle business when Gaal and his people step out.'
9.34: So Abimelech and his troops set up at night, lying in wait in four groups outside Shechem.
9.35: Early in the morning, Gaal walked to the city gates, and Abimelech's troops popped up out of nowhere.
9.36: Gaal saw them and told Zebul, 'Yo, look! People coming down from the mountains!'
9.37: Gaal looked again: 'Nah, I'm telling you, people are coming down from the middle of the land! And another squad is rolling up from the Diviner's Tree!'
9.38: Zebul hit him back: 'Where's all that big talk now? You was talking reckless about Abimelech—now go fight him!'
9.39: So Gaal led Shechem's men out to fight Abimelech.
9.40: Abimelech chased him down, and Gaal's men got wrecked all the way back to the city gates.
9.41: Abimelech stayed at Arumah while Zebul kicked Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
9.42: Next day, Shechem's people went out to the fields, and somebody told Abimelech.
9.43: He set another ambush, split his men into three groups, and attacked when they came out.
9.44: Abimelech and his squad stormed the city gates while the other two squads hit everyone still in the fields.
9.45: He fought Shechem all day, took the city, killed everyone inside, tore it down, and scattered salt all over it.
9.46: When the people in Shechem's tower heard what happened, they ran to the temple of their false god, Berith.
9.47: But Abimelech found out they were hiding there.
9.48: He and his troops went to Mount Zalmon. Abimelech chopped a tree branch, put it on his shoulder, and said, 'Y'all see what I just did? Do the same thing!'
9.49: So everybody grabbed branches, stacked them around the temple, and set it on fire. About a thousand men and women burned alive.
9.50: Then Abimelech went to Thebez, took over the city.
9.51: But the people ran into a strong tower, locked themselves in, and climbed to the roof.
9.52: Abimelech rushed the tower and was about to set it on fire.
9.53: But a random woman dropped a millstone on his head and cracked his skull!
9.54: Abimelech, not wanting to die by a woman's hand, told his armor-bearer, 'Run me through with your sword! I can't go out like this!' So the young man killed him.
9.55: When the Israelites saw Abimelech was dead, they all went home.
9.56: That's how God paid back Abimelech for killing his seventy brothers.
9.57: And all the evil Shechem did came back on them too. Everything played out just like Jotham said.

10.1: After Abimelech, a man named Tola, son of Puah, grandson of Dodo, from the tribe of Issachar, stepped up to save Israel. He lived in Shamir, up in the hills of Ephraim.
10.2: Tola judged Israel for 23 years. Then he died and was buried in Shamir.
10.3: After Tola, a man named Jair, a Gileadite, became judge over Israel. He led for 22 years.
10.4: Jair had thirty sons, and they was out here riding thirty donkeys. Each one of them had their own town, which they called 'Havoth Jair'—the Villages of Jair. That name still sticks to this day in Gilead.
10.5: Then Jair died and was buried in Camon.
10.6: But, like clockwork, Israel started wildin' again—doing evil in the Lord's sight. They was out here serving every god they could find: Baal, Ashtoreth, the gods of Syria, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and the Philistines. Straight up forgot about the Lord.
10.7: So the Lord got fed up and let the Philistines and the Ammonites run all over them.
10.8: For 18 years, these enemies harassed and oppressed Israel, especially the folks living in Gilead, the land of the Amorites.
10.9: Then the Ammonites got even bolder and crossed the Jordan, bringing the fight to Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Israel was struggling heavy.
10.10: Finally, Israel cried out to the Lord, saying, 'We messed up, Lord! We abandoned You and started serving these fake gods!'
10.11: But the Lord hit them back with, 'Didn't I save y'all before? I pulled y'all out of Egypt, rescued you from the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines.'
10.12: 'I saved y'all from the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites when they oppressed you. Every time y'all cried out, I came through.'
10.13: 'But y'all keep ditching Me for these other gods. So nah, I ain't saving y'all no more.'
10.14: 'Matter fact, go cry to them gods y'all love so much. Let's see if they pull up for you when you in trouble.'
10.15: But Israel pleaded, 'Lord, we messed up! Do whatever You gotta do to us, but please, just save us today!'
10.16: So they threw out all their fake gods and started serving the Lord again. And God—seeing how much they was suffering—couldn't ignore their misery no more.
10.17: Meanwhile, the Ammonites gathered their army and camped in Gilead. Israel's people came together too, setting up camp in Mizpah.
10.18: Then the leaders of Gilead started talking: 'Who gon' be the one to lead us against the Ammonites? Whoever steps up first gon' be the ruler over all of Gilead.'

11.1: Jephthah, the Gileadite, was a straight-up warrior, but his mom was a prostitute. His father, Gilead, had him outside of marriage.
11.2: When Gilead's legit sons grew up, they told Jephthah, 'Bruh, you ain't getting nothing from this family. You the son of another woman—get out.'
11.3: So Jephthah left and went to live in the land of Tob. While he was there, a bunch of reckless dudes linked up with him, and they started rolling together like a gang.
11.4: Some time passed, and the Ammonites started beefing with Israel again.
11.5: When war broke out, the elders of Gilead went looking for Jephthah in Tob.
11.6: They said, 'Come be our commander so we can fight the Ammonites!'
11.7: But Jephthah was like, 'Oh now y'all need me? Ain't y'all the same ones that kicked me out my daddy's house? Now y'all in trouble and suddenly I'm important?'
11.8: The elders were like, 'Yeah… that's why we came back to you. Lead us in battle, and you can be the head over all of Gilead.'
11.9: Jephthah said, 'So if I come back, lead the fight, and God gives me the victory, y'all really gon' make me the ruler?'
11.10: They swore on it, saying, 'The Lord is our witness—we'll do exactly what we said.'
11.11: So Jephthah went with them, and the people made him their leader. Then Jephthah made it official before the Lord in Mizpah.
11.12: Jephthah sent messengers to the king of Ammon, asking, 'Yo, why you pulling up on my land trying to fight me?'
11.13: The Ammonite king responded, 'Y'all took our land when you came from Egypt—from the Arnon to the Jabbok and over to the Jordan. Give it back peacefully, and we won't have a problem.'
11.15: 'Israel never took Moab's land or Ammon's land.'
11.16: 'When Israel left Egypt, they wandered the wilderness, passed through the Red Sea, and came to Kadesh.'
11.17: 'They asked Edom's king, "Can we pass through your land?" but he said no. They asked Moab's king, same thing—no entry. So they had to stay put in Kadesh.'
11.18: 'Then they went around Edom and Moab and camped near the Arnon River, but never crossed into Moab's land.'
11.19: 'Then they asked Sihon, king of the Amorites, "Let us pass through your land to get where we going."'
11.20: 'But Sihon wasn't having it. Instead, he came at Israel with his whole army, ready to fight.'
11.21: 'But the Lord handed Sihon and his people over to Israel, and we took all their land.'
11.22: 'From the Arnon to the Jabbok, from the wilderness to the Jordan—it all became ours.'
11.23: 'So if God took this land from the Amorites and gave it to us, why should we give it to you?'
11.24: 'Y'all keep what your god Chemosh gives you, and we gon' keep what our God gives us.'
11.25: 'Are you better than Balak, Moab's king? He never picked a fight with Israel.'
11.26: 'Israel been living in Heshbon, Aroer, and along the Arnon for 300 years—why y'all just now trying to claim it?'
11.27: 'I ain't the one in the wrong. You are. So let the Lord judge between us today!'
11.28: But the Ammonite king ignored Jephthah's message.
11.29: Then the Spirit of the Lord came on Jephthah. He traveled through Gilead and Manasseh, then passed through Mizpah on his way to fight Ammon.
11.30: Before the battle, Jephthah made a vow to the Lord: 'If You let me win, Lord…'
11.31: 'Whatever comes out my house first when I get back, I'ma give it to You as a burnt offering.'
11.32: Jephthah led his army against the Ammonites, and the Lord gave him the victory.
11.33: He wiped them out from Aroer to Minnith—twenty cities—reaching Abel Keramim. It was a brutal defeat, and Ammon fell under Israel.
11.34: But when Jephthah came home to Mizpah, his only child—his daughter—ran out to greet him with tambourines, dancing.
11.35: When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried out, 'Nooo! My daughter! You just broke me down! I made a vow to the Lord, and I can't take it back!'
11.36: She told him, 'Daddy, if you made a vow to the Lord, you gotta keep it—since He gave you the victory over your enemies.'
11.37: 'But let me have two months to go into the mountains with my friends and mourn the fact that I'll never have a husband or kids.'
11.38: Jephthah agreed. 'Go ahead.' So she and her friends spent two months mourning in the mountains.
11.39: After that, she came back, and Jephthah fulfilled his vow. She never married or had children.
11.40: From then on, the daughters of Israel set aside four days each year to remember Jephthah's daughter.

12.1: The men of Ephraim got together, crossed over to Zaphon, and came at Jephthah like, 'Bruh, why you go fight Ammon without us? You ain't call us? We 'bout to burn your house down with you in it!'
12.2: Jephthah clapped back, 'Look, me and my people was struggling against Ammon. I did call y'all, but y'all ain't come help.'
12.3: 'So when I saw y'all wasn't coming, I risked my own life, went to fight Ammon, and the Lord gave me the W. So why y'all pulling up on me now?'
12.4: Then Jephthah and his Gileadite soldiers went to war against Ephraim and beat them, 'cause Ephraim was talking reckless, saying, 'Y'all Gileadites are just Ephraimite runaways—y'all ain't real.'
12.5: After the battle, the Gileadites took control of the Jordan River crossings. Anytime an Ephraimite tried to escape and said, 'Let me cross over,' the Gileadites would ask, 'You an Ephraimite?'
12.6: If the person said no, they'd make him say, 'Shibboleth.' If he couldn't pronounce it right and said, 'Sibboleth,' they knew he was lying and would take him out right there. 42,000 Ephraimites died that day.
12.7: Jephthah judged Israel for six years. Then he died and was buried somewhere in Gilead.
12.8: After Jephthah, Ibzan from Bethlehem took over as judge.
12.9: This dude had thirty sons, gave away thirty daughters in marriage, and brought in thirty daughters for his sons. He judged Israel for seven years.
12.10: Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
12.11: Next up was Elon from the tribe of Zebulun. He judged Israel for ten years.
12.12: Then Elon died and was buried in Aijalon, in the land of Zebulun.
12.13: After him came Abdon, son of Hillel, from Pirathon.
12.14: He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, and all of them rode around on seventy donkeys. He judged Israel for eight years.
12.15: Then Abdon died and was buried in Pirathon, in Ephraim, in the hill country where the Amalekites used to be.

13.1: Once again, Israel started acting up, doing evil in the Lord's sight. So the Lord let the Philistines run them for forty years.
13.2: There was this man from Zorah, from the tribe of Dan, named Manoah. His wife couldn't have kids.
13.3: Then the Angel of the Lord pulled up and told her, 'Look, I know you ain't been able to have kids, but you 'bout to have a son.'
13.4: 'So listen up—don't drink no wine, don't touch strong drinks, and don't eat anything unclean.'
13.5: 'This baby gon' be special. No razor should ever touch his head, 'cause he's gonna be dedicated to God as a Nazirite from birth. And he's the one that's gonna start rescuing Israel from the Philistines.'
13.6: The woman ran and told her husband, 'A Man of God came to me! He looked like an angel—real powerful. I ain't ask where He came from, and He ain't tell me His name.'
13.7: 'But He told me, "You gon' have a son. Don't drink wine, don't eat nothing unclean, 'cause this child is dedicated to God from the womb until he dies."'
13.8: Then Manoah prayed, 'Lord, please send that Man of God back so we can know exactly how to raise this child.'
13.9: God heard him, and the Angel of the Lord showed up again while his wife was out in the field. But Manoah wasn't with her.
13.10: She ran back, found her husband, and said, 'He's back! The Man who talked to me the other day just appeared again!'
13.11: Manoah followed her, came up to the Man, and asked, 'Are you the one who spoke to my wife?' And He said, 'I am.'
13.12: Manoah said, 'Alright then, let everything You said happen! But tell us—how we supposed to raise this boy? What's his purpose?'
13.13: The Angel of the Lord said, 'She gotta follow everything I told her.'
13.14: 'No wine, no strong drinks, nothing unclean—she gotta stick to all My instructions.'
13.15: Then Manoah said, 'Please, stay for a while. Let us prepare a young goat for You.'
13.16: But the Angel of the Lord said, 'Even if I stay, I ain't eating your food. But if you want to make an offering, give it to the Lord.' (Manoah still ain't realize this was the Angel of the Lord.)
13.17: Then Manoah asked, 'What's Your name? That way, when everything You said comes true, we can honor You.'
13.18: But the Angel of the Lord said, 'Why you asking My name? It's beyond understanding—it's wonderful.'
13.19: So Manoah took a young goat and a grain offering, sacrificed it on a rock to the Lord. And while they were watching, something amazing happened.
13.20: As the flames rose up to heaven, the Angel of the Lord went up in the fire! When Manoah and his wife saw it, they fell flat on their faces.
13.21: After that, the Angel of the Lord disappeared. That's when Manoah realized, 'Oh snap, that was the Angel of the Lord for real!'
13.22: Then he freaked out, telling his wife, 'We 'bout to die! We just saw God!'
13.23: But his wife was calm and said, 'If the Lord wanted us dead, He wouldn't have accepted our offering. He wouldn't have shown us all this or told us what's about to happen.'
13.24: Then she gave birth to a son and named him Samson. The boy grew up, and the Lord blessed him.
13.25: And the Spirit of the Lord started working in him while he was at Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

14.1: One day, Samson went down to Timnah and saw a Philistine woman that caught his eye.
14.2: He came back home and told his parents, 'I saw this fine woman in Timnah—one of the Philistine girls. Go ahead and set that up for me as my wife.'
14.3: His parents were like, 'Hold up, ain't there no woman from our own people you can marry? Why you gotta go after one of these uncircumcised Philistines?' But Samson was like, 'Nah, she the one I want. Go get her for me.'
14.4: What his parents ain't know was that the Lord was behind this, setting things up to bring trouble to the Philistines—since they were still running Israel at the time.
14.5: So Samson and his folks headed down to Timnah. Along the way, near the vineyards, a young lion jumped out at him, roaring.
14.6: But the Spirit of the Lord hit Samson with crazy strength, and he tore that lion apart with his bare hands—like it was nothing! He ain't even have a weapon. But he ain't tell his parents what happened.
14.7: After that, he went to talk with the Philistine woman, and yeah—he was feeling her heavy.
14.8: Later on, when he came back to get her, he decided to check out the lion's carcass. And what did he see? A whole beehive inside, with honey dripping.
14.9: He scooped some up and ate it on the way. When he got to his parents, he gave them some too, but he ain't tell them where it came from.
14.10: His father went ahead and arranged the marriage. Samson threw a feast, like young men usually did in those days.
14.11: When the Philistines saw Samson, they brought thirty men to hang with him—basically like wedding guests.
14.12: Then Samson told them, 'Aight, let's make this fun. I got a riddle for y'all. If you can solve it in the seven days of the feast, I'll give y'all thirty linen garments and thirty fresh outfits.'
14.13: 'But if y'all can't solve it, y'all gotta give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.' They were like, 'Aight, bet. Hit us with the riddle.'
14.14: So Samson said, 'Out of the eater came something to eat, And out of the strong came something sweet.' But for three days, they was stuck—they had no clue what the answer was.
14.15: By the seventh day, they was getting mad. So they went to Samson's wife and told her, 'You better get your husband to tell you the answer, or we burning you and your daddy's house down! You brought us here just to rob us?'
14.16: So Samson's wife started crying on him, saying, 'You don't love me! You hate me! You made this riddle for my people, but you ain't even tell me the answer!' But Samson was like, 'Girl, I ain't even tell my parents! Why would I tell you?'
14.17: But she kept crying. The whole feast, she was pressing him. By the seventh day, he gave in and told her. And of course, she ran straight to her people with the answer.
14.18: So before the sun went down, the Philistine men came to Samson and said, 'What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?' And Samson was heated. He snapped back, 'If y'all ain't been messing with my wife, Y'all wouldn't have solved my riddle!'
14.19: The Spirit of the Lord came on Samson again, and he went down to Ashkelon, killed thirty Philistine men, took their clothes, and gave them to the men who solved the riddle. But he was still mad, so he stormed off back to his father's house.
14.20: And while he was gone, Samson's wife was given to his best man instead!

15.1: Sometime later, during the wheat harvest, Samson pulled up to see his wife, bringing a young goat as a gift. He was like, 'Aight, let me go see my wife in her room.' But her dad blocked the door.
15.2: Her father said, 'Look, I really thought you was done with her, so I gave her to your boy. But hey, ain't her younger sister even finer? Take her instead.'
15.3: Samson was heated. He said, 'Aight, this time, when I get back at the Philistines, y'all can't blame me!'
15.4: So Samson caught 300 foxes, tied them together in pairs by their tails, and strapped torches between them.
15.5: Then he lit the torches and let the foxes loose in the Philistine fields, burning up all their grain, vineyards, and olive groves.
15.6: The Philistines were like, 'Who did this?!' And somebody told them, 'It was Samson, that Timnite's son-in-law, 'cause his father-in-law gave his wife to another dude.' So the Philistines came through and burned both Samson's wife and her father alive.
15.7: Samson snapped, 'Oh, y'all wanna play like that? Aight, bet—I will get my revenge, and after that, I'm done.'
15.8: Then he ran through them, wrecking everybody, taking them down left and right. After that, he dipped to a cave in the rock of Etam.
15.9: The Philistines rolled up, set up camp in Judah, and prepared to take over Lehi.
15.10: The men of Judah asked, 'Yo, why y'all here?' The Philistines said, 'We came to arrest Samson and do to him what he did to us.'
15.11: So 3,000 men from Judah went to Samson's hideout in the cave and said, 'Bruh, you know the Philistines run this place! Why you bringing trouble on us?!' Samson said, 'Man, I just did to them what they did to me.'
15.12: They told him, 'Look, we gotta turn you in to them.' Samson said, 'Fine, but swear to me that y'all won't kill me yourselves.'
15.13: They promised, 'Nah, we just tying you up and handing you over—we ain't gon' kill you.' So they tied him up with two fresh ropes and led him out.
15.14: As soon as they brought Samson to Lehi, the Philistines saw him and started shouting like they already won. But the Spirit of the Lord hit Samson with power—the ropes around his arms snapped like burnt thread, and his hands broke free like nothing.
15.15: He looked around, grabbed a fresh donkey's jawbone, and went crazy—took out a thousand men with it.
15.16: Then Samson said, 'With a donkey's jawbone, I stacked 'em in heaps, With a donkey's jawbone, I just took out a thousand men!'
15.17: After he finished, he tossed the jawbone and called that spot Ramath Lehi (which means 'Jawbone Hill').
15.18: After all that, Samson was mad thirsty, so he prayed, 'Lord, You just gave me this big victory, and now I'm 'bout to die of thirst and get caught by these uncircumcised dudes?'
15.19: So God made water flow from a hollow place in Lehi. Samson drank, got his strength back, and felt revived. That place was called En Hakkore ('Spring of the Caller'), and the name stuck.
15.20: And Samson judged Israel for twenty years while the Philistines were still in charge.

16.1: Samson went down to Gaza, saw a prostitute, and spent the night with her.
16.2: When the people of Gaza found out, they were like, 'Oh, Samson in town? Bet. We gon' wait for him all night, and when the morning comes, we gon' kill him.'
16.3: But Samson laid low until midnight. Then he got up, grabbed the city gate doors—posts, bars, and all—ripped them out the ground, threw them on his shoulders, and carried them all the way to the top of a hill near Hebron.
16.4: Sometime later, Samson fell for a woman in the Valley of Sorek named Delilah.
16.5: The Philistine leaders came to her and said, 'Find out what makes him so strong and how we can take him down. We wanna tie him up and make him suffer. Each of us will give you 1,100 pieces of silver if you do it.'
16.6: So Delilah started working on him, saying, 'Baby, tell me the secret to your strength. How can someone tie you up and make you weak?'
16.7: Samson played with her and said, 'If they tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings that haven't dried, I'll be weak like any other man.'
16.8: So the Philistine leaders brought her the bowstrings, and she tied him up.
16.9: Then she had men hiding in the room, and she called out, 'Samson! The Philistines are here!' But he snapped those bowstrings like they was nothing, and they still ain't know his secret.
16.10: Delilah got mad and said, 'You lied to me! Tell me the real way to tie you up.'
16.11: Samson said, 'If they tie me with brand-new ropes that ain't never been used, then I'll be weak like anybody else.'
16.12: So Delilah tied him up with new ropes and called out, 'Samson! The Philistines are here!' But he broke the ropes like thread.
16.13: Delilah was real fed up now: 'You keep playing with me, Samson! Tell me the truth!' So Samson said, 'Alright, alright. If you weave the seven braids of my hair into a loom, I'll be weak.'
16.14: So she did it, pinned it down, and shouted, 'Samson! The Philistines are here!' But he woke up, pulled the pin out, and broke free again.
16.15: Delilah hit him with, 'How you gon' say you love me, but you keep lying?'
16.16: She kept nagging him day after day until he was fed up with her pressing him.
16.17: So he finally broke and told her everything: 'I've been dedicated to God since birth as a Nazirite. If my head ever gets shaved, I'll lose my strength and be weak like any other man.'
16.18: Delilah knew this time was real. She called the Philistine leaders and said, 'Come on, this time he told me everything!' And they came back with the silver in their hands.
16.19: She made him fall asleep on her lap, then called a man to shave off his seven braids. Then she started messing with him, and his strength was gone.
16.20: She yelled, 'Samson! The Philistines are here!' He woke up thinking, 'I'ma break free like before.' But he ain't know the Lord had left him.
16.21: The Philistines grabbed him, gouged out his eyes, dragged him to Gaza, and put him in prison, making him grind grain like a slave.
16.22: But while he was locked up, his hair started growing back…
16.23: One day, the Philistine rulers threw a big party to worship their god, Dagon. They were hyped, saying, 'Our god gave us victory over Samson!'
16.24: The people celebrated, saying, 'Samson, the one who wrecked our land and killed our people, is finally in our hands!'
16.25: When they got drunk, they said, 'Bring out Samson so he can entertain us!' So they pulled him out the prison and put him on display.
16.26: Samson said to the boy guiding him, 'Take me to the pillars holding up the temple so I can lean on them.'
16.27: The temple was packed—3,000 men and women, including all the Philistine rulers, were watching from the roof.
16.28: Samson prayed, 'Lord God, remember me. Please, just one more time—give me the strength to get revenge for my two eyes!'
16.29: He grabbed the two central pillars holding up the temple, put one hand on each, and braced himself.
16.30: Then he said, 'Let me die with these Philistines!' And he pushed with all his might. The whole temple came crashing down, killing everyone inside—including Samson. In that moment, he killed more Philistines in death than he ever did in life.
16.31: Later, his brothers and family came, took his body, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol, in his father Manoah's tomb. He had led Israel for twenty years.

17.1: There was this man named Micah, living up in the mountains of Ephraim.
17.2: One day, he told his mom, 'Remember them eleven hundred pieces of silver that got stolen from you? The ones you put a curse on—yeah, I took them.' But his mom ain't even mad. She said, 'May the Lord bless you, my son!'
17.3: So after he gave the money back, she said, 'I had dedicated this silver to the Lord for you—so we could make a carved idol and a molded statue. Now, I'm giving it back to you to make it happen.'
17.4: So Micah returned the money, and his mom took two hundred shekels, gave them to a silversmith, and had him make an idol. They put it in Micah's house.
17.5: Micah even built a little shrine, made an ephod (a priestly vest), and set up some household gods. Then he ordained one of his own sons to be his priest.
17.6: Back then, Israel ain't have no king—everybody was just doing whatever they thought was right.
17.7: Now there was a young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, looking for a place to stay.
17.8: He left Bethlehem, just trying to find a spot where he could settle down. While traveling, he came to Micah's house in the mountains of Ephraim.
17.9: Micah asked him, 'Where you from?' And the young man said, 'I'm a Levite from Bethlehem, just out here looking for a place to stay.'
17.10: Micah said, 'Aight, stay with me. Be my priest and my spiritual leader. I'll hook you up with ten pieces of silver a year, a fresh set of clothes, and everything you need.'
17.11: The Levite agreed, moved in, and became like a son to Micah.
17.12: Micah then ordained him as his personal priest, and the Levite stayed in Micah's house.
17.13: Micah was hyped. He said, 'Now I know the Lord gon' bless me—I got a legit Levite as my priest!'

18.1: Back in those days, Israel ain't have no king, and the tribe of Dan was still out here looking for land to claim for themselves.
18.2: So the Danites sent five strong men from Zorah and Eshtaol to scout out a new spot. They told them, 'Go check out the land and report back.' As they traveled, they stopped at Micah's house in the mountains of Ephraim and stayed the night.
18.3: While they were there, they overheard the Levite priest talking and recognized his accent. So they asked, 'Yo, who brought you here? What you doing in this place?'
18.4: He told them, 'Oh, Micah hired me. I'm his personal priest now.'
18.5: So the men said, 'Aight, can you ask God if this trip gon' be a success?'
18.6: The priest told them, 'Yeah, y'all good. The Lord got you on this journey.'
18.7: So the five men went on to Laish. They saw that the people there were chill—living peaceful, like the Sidonians, without no rulers pressing them. Plus, they ain't have any strong allies to back them up.
18.8: When the spies got back to Zorah and Eshtaol, their people asked, 'So what's the word?'
18.9: They said, 'Man, we gotta move! This land is real nice. Why y'all just sitting here? Let's go take it!'
18.10: 'The people there ain't got no defenses, and the land is stacked with everything we could want. God already gave it to us!'
18.11: So 600 armed men from the tribe of Dan left from Zorah and Eshtaol, ready for war.
18.12: On the way, they camped at Kirjath Jearim in Judah, and that spot became known as Mahaneh Dan (which means 'Camp of Dan').
18.13: Then they continued through the mountains of Ephraim and stopped at Micah's house.
18.14: The five spies told the rest of the group, 'Yo, y'all know Micah got an ephod, household idols, a carved image, and a molded statue, right? We need to do something about that.'
18.15: So they rolled up to Micah's house and greeted the young Levite priest.
18.16: Meanwhile, the 600 armed Danites were posted up at the entrance of the gate.
18.17: The five spies went inside and straight-up stole the carved idol, ephod, household gods, and molded image, while the priest stood outside with the warriors.
18.18: When the priest saw them taking everything, he asked, 'Bruh, what y'all doing?'
18.19: They told him, 'Look, be quiet and come with us. You wanna be a priest for one man, or you wanna be a priest for an entire tribe of Israel? Think about it—this is an upgrade!'
18.20: The priest thought about it, and he was real happy. He grabbed the idols and joined them.
18.21: Then the Danites took off, putting their families, livestock, and goods up front.
18.22: After they got some distance, Micah and some of his neighbors caught up to the Danites.
18.23: They shouted at them, and the Danites turned around, saying, 'Why you pressing us? What's the problem?'
18.24: Micah said, 'Y'all stole my gods and my priest, and now you asking me what the problem is? Bruh, y'all took everything from me!'
18.25: The Danites responded, 'Look, keep your voice down before one of these hotheads gets mad and you end up dead—your whole household too.'
18.26: Micah saw they had him outnumbered, so he just turned around and went home.
18.27: The Danites took Micah's idols and priest, went to Laish, and attacked. They wiped out the peaceful people there with the sword and burned the whole city down.
18.28: Nobody came to save them, 'cause they was too far from Sidon and had no alliances. After that, the Danites rebuilt the city and moved in.
18.29: They renamed the city Dan, after their ancestor. But before that, it was called Laish.
18.30: Then the Danites set up Micah's idol and made Jonathan, the son of Gershom (Moses' grandson), and his sons the tribe's priests. They stayed in that role until Israel got taken into captivity.
18.31: So the Danites kept Micah's idol with them the whole time, even though the true house of God was in Shiloh.

19.1: Back in those days, Israel ain't have no king. There was this Levite living up in the remote mountains of Ephraim, and he had a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.
19.2: But she wasn't loyal—she stepped out on him, then ran off to her daddy's house in Bethlehem, staying there for four months.
19.3: After a while, her husband decided to go get her. He wanted to talk to her nice and bring her back. He pulled up with his servant and two donkeys. When she saw him, she took him into her father's house. Her father was happy to meet him.
19.4: Her dad convinced him to stay for three days, so they ate, drank, and kicked it.
19.5: On the fourth day, the Levite got up early to leave, but his father-in-law said, 'Hold up, eat something first, get your strength up, then y'all can go.'
19.6: So they sat down, ate, and drank together. Then her dad was like, 'You should stay another night, have a good time.'
19.7: When the Levite got up to leave, his father-in-law insisted he stay again. So he stayed another night.
19.8: Next morning, he got up early to leave, but her dad said, 'Come on, eat first, take your time.' So they ended up chilling till the afternoon, eating and drinking again.
19.9: When the Levite got up again to leave with his concubine and servant, her father said, 'Look, it's getting late. Just stay one more night and leave early tomorrow.'
19.10: But the Levite was done waiting. He took his concubine and left, making it as far as Jebus (which is Jerusalem). His two donkeys were saddled, and they kept it moving.
19.11: As the sun was going down, his servant said, 'Master, let's stop here in Jebus and stay the night.'
19.12: But the Levite said, 'Nah, we ain't staying in no foreign city with people who ain't Israelites. We'll go to Gibeah.'
19.13: 'Matter of fact, let's try to make it to Gibeah or Ramah before we stop for the night.'
19.14: They kept walking, but the sun went down when they reached Gibeah, which was in the land of Benjamin.
19.15: So they stopped there, but nobody in town offered them a place to stay, so they just sat in the city square.
19.16: Then, an old man came in from working in the fields. He was from Ephraim but lived in Gibeah, unlike the Benjamites who ran the place.
19.17: He saw the travelers and asked, 'Where y'all coming from? Where y'all headed?'
19.18: The Levite answered, 'We're coming from Bethlehem, heading back to my home in Ephraim. But nobody here is offering us a place to stay.'
19.19: 'We got food, wine, straw for our donkeys—everything we need. We just need a place to rest.'
19.20: The old man said, 'Y'all good. I got you. Just don't sleep in the square.'
19.21: So he took them to his house, fed their donkeys, and they washed up, ate, and drank.
19.22: While they were relaxing, some wicked men from the city came and surrounded the house. They started banging on the door and shouted to the old man, 'Bring out that traveler! We wanna know him!'
19.23: The old man stepped outside and said, 'Nah, my brothers! Don't do this evil thing. This man is a guest in my house—don't bring this shame on us!'
19.24: 'Look, take my daughter, she's a virgin, and take his concubine—do whatever you want to them, but don't do this wickedness to this man!'
19.25: But the men weren't trying to hear it. So the Levite grabbed his concubine and threw her outside to them. They assaulted her all night, abusing her until the morning. At sunrise, they finally let her go.
19.26: As the sun rose, she barely made it back to the house, collapsed at the door, and laid there with her hands stretched toward the threshold.
19.27: Her master got up in the morning, opened the door to leave, and saw her lying there. He said, 'Get up, let's go.' But she ain't answer.
19.28: So he picked her up, put her on his donkey, and took her home.
19.29: When he got home, he grabbed a knife, took his concubine's body, and cut her into twelve pieces. Then he sent one piece to each tribe of Israel.
19.30: Everybody who saw it was shook. They said, 'Ain't nothing like this ever happened in Israel—not since we left Egypt! We gotta talk about this. We need to figure out what to do!'

20.1: All the Israelites, from Dan to Beersheba and even Gilead, came together like one squad before the Lord at Mizpah.
20.2: The leaders from every tribe showed up, and 400,000 soldiers ready for battle stood together.
20.3: Meanwhile, the tribe of Benjamin got word that Israel was gathering at Mizpah.
20.4: The Levite—the one whose concubine was murdered—stood up and said, 'Me and my concubine went to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.'
20.5: 'But the men of Gibeah surrounded the house, ready to kill me, and instead, they assaulted my concubine until she died.'
20.6: 'So I cut up her body and sent the pieces all over Israel, because this was an evil crime against our people!'
20.7: 'Now y'all tell me—what are we gonna do about it?'
20.8: Everybody agreed: 'We ain't going home till we handle this.'
20.9: 'Here's the plan: We're taking Gibeah down. We'll divide our forces and make sure justice gets served.'
20.10: 'We'll send out ten percent of our men to gather supplies so that when we move on Gibeah, we'll be ready to make them pay for this wickedness.'
20.11: So all of Israel stood together, ready to wipe Gibeah off the map.
20.12: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to the Benjamites, saying, 'What's up with this wickedness happening in Gibeah?'
20.13: 'Hand over the ones who did this so we can put them to death and remove this evil from Israel!' But Benjamin refused to listen to their own kin.
20.14: Instead of handling the guilty men, the Benjamites gathered their own army from different cities and got ready to fight Israel.
20.15: They had 26,000 soldiers, plus 700 elite fighters from Gibeah.
20.16: These 700 men were left-handed sharpshooters who could sling a stone and hit a target without missing.
20.17: Meanwhile, the Israelites had 400,000 trained soldiers.
20.18: Before going into battle, Israel went to the house of God and asked, 'Lord, who should go up first against Benjamin?' The Lord said, 'Judah first!'
20.19: So Israel camped near Gibeah and got ready.
20.20: When the fight started, Israel lined up against Benjamin.
20.21: But the Benjamites came out swinging, and that day, they killed 22,000 Israelites.
20.22: Israel's men regrouped and got back in position, refusing to give up.
20.23: They went back to the Lord, weeping and asking, 'Should we fight our brothers again?' The Lord said, 'Yes, go back to battle.'
20.24: So they fought again the next day.
20.25: But this time, Benjamin struck down another 18,000 Israelite soldiers.
20.26: After losing twice, all of Israel went before the Lord, crying, fasting, and offering sacrifices.
20.27: At that time, the Ark of the Covenant was still in Israel, and Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron, was the high priest.
20.28: Israel asked again, 'Lord, should we keep fighting or stop?' And the Lord said, 'Go again. Tomorrow, I'll hand them over to you.'
20.29: This time, Israel set up an ambush around Gibeah.
20.30: On the third day, Israel attacked just like before, lining up for battle.
20.31: The Benjamites thought they had the upper hand again, so they rushed out, striking down some Israelites on the highways and in the fields.
20.32: They thought, 'We got 'em just like before!' But Israel was setting a trap.
20.33: Israel's soldiers pulled back, drawing the Benjamites away from the city. Then the hidden ambush unit rushed in and attacked Gibeah.
20.34: The battle got real intense, and Benjamin didn't even realize disaster was coming for them.
20.35: This time, the Lord handed Benjamin over to Israel. They wiped out 25,100 Benjamite soldiers.
20.36: The Benjamites saw they were losing and tried to retreat.
20.37: Meanwhile, the Israelite ambush team stormed Gibeah, slaughtered the city, and burned it down.
20.38: They had set a signal—once a huge smoke cloud rose from the city, the Israelite army would know the ambush was complete.
20.39: At first, the Benjamites thought they were winning, taking down some Israelites. But when they looked back and saw the smoke rising, they panicked.
20.40: That's when they knew—it was over.
20.41: The Israelites turned back and attacked full force. The Benjamites realized disaster had hit.
20.42: They tried to run toward the wilderness, but Israel chased them down, cutting them down wherever they ran.
20.43: They surrounded them, trapping them in a deadly battle that spread east toward Gibeah.
20.44: By the time it was over, 18,000 Benjamite warriors were dead.
20.45: The survivors ran for their lives toward the wilderness at Rimmon Rock, but Israel kept chasing. They cut down another 5,000 on the highways, then another 2,000 at Gidom.
20.46: In total, 25,000 Benjamites died that day—elite warriors who fought to the end.
20.47: Only 600 Benjamites made it out alive, escaping to Rimmon Rock, where they hid for four months.
20.48: Meanwhile, Israel went through all the Benjamite towns, destroying everything—men, livestock, and cities. They set fire to everything they found.

21.1: The men of Israel had made a serious oath at Mizpah, saying, 'Ain't none of us giving our daughters to Benjamin as wives.'
21.2: Then the people came to the house of God and stayed there till evening, crying out loud and weeping hard.
21.3: They said, 'Lord, how did it come to this? How did we end up losing a whole tribe of Israel today?'
21.4: The next morning, they got up early, built an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to God.
21.5: Then they asked, 'Who from Israel ain't show up when we gathered at Mizpah? 'Cause we swore that anybody who ain't show up should be put to death.'
21.6: The Israelites were grieving hard for Benjamin, saying, 'One of our own tribes is about to disappear—what we supposed to do?'
21.7: 'How we gon' find wives for the few that's left, since we already swore not to give them our daughters?'
21.8: Then they asked, 'Wait, which tribe ain't come to Mizpah?' Turns out, nobody from Jabesh Gilead had shown up.
21.9: When they did a headcount, they realized not one single person from Jabesh Gilead had come to the gathering.
21.10: So Israel sent 12,000 of their best warriors and told them, 'Go to Jabesh Gilead and wipe 'em out—kill all the men and every woman who's already been with a man.'
21.11: 'Take out every male and every married woman.'
21.12: They ended up finding 400 young virgins who hadn't been with a man. They brought them back to the camp at Shiloh in Canaan.
21.13: Then the whole congregation sent messengers to the surviving Benjamites hiding at Rimmon Rock, letting them know they could come back in peace.
21.14: So Benjamin returned, and Israel gave them the women they had taken from Jabesh Gilead. But it still wasn't enough.
21.15: The people were hurting, 'cause they knew the Lord had allowed this tribe to be nearly wiped out.
21.16: The elders asked, 'What we gon' do for the rest of these men? They need wives, and all the women of Benjamin are gone.'
21.17: 'We gotta make sure Benjamin don't disappear completely—every tribe needs an inheritance.'
21.18: 'But we can't give them our daughters, 'cause we swore an oath against that.'
21.19: Then somebody had an idea: 'Wait a minute—there's that yearly festival of the Lord in Shiloh. The one north of Bethel, near the road that leads to Shechem.'
21.20: So they told the remaining Benjamites, 'Here's what y'all gon' do: Hide out in the vineyards near Shiloh.'
21.21: 'When the young women come out to dance for the festival, jump out, grab a wife, and take her back to Benjamin!'
21.22: 'And when their fathers and brothers complain, we'll tell them, "Look, just let it slide. Y'all ain't really 'give' them to Benjamin, so technically, you ain't breaking your oath."'
21.23: So the Benjamites did exactly that—when the young women of Shiloh came out dancing, they grabbed enough wives for themselves, then went back home to rebuild their cities.
21.24: After that, everybody went back to their own tribes and homes, returning to their land and inheritance.
21.25: Back in those days, Israel ain't have no king—everybody just did whatever they thought was right.
